content.text: I'm looking at `InputStreamReadStream`. It uses `vertx.getOrCreateContext()` and `vertx.executeBlocking`, which may not stay on the caller's Vert.x context. I'll pin it to one context.

s=s.replace("        this.vertx = vertx;\n","        this.vertx = vertx;\n        // capture the context that issued the request so that all callbacks stay on it\n        this.context = vertx.getOrCreateContext();\n")
s=s.replace("new InboundBuffer<>(vertx.getOrCreateContext())","new InboundBuffer<>(context)")
s=s.replace("vertx.runOnContext(v -> readChunk());","context.runOnContext(v -> readChunk());")
s=s.replace("vertx.executeBlocking(() ->","context.executeBlocking(() ->")
open(f,"w").write(s)
E

content.text:
I changed `InputStreamReadStream` in `independent-projects/resteasy-reactive/client/runtime/.../client/impl/`. It now captures one Vert.x `Context` in its constructor and uses it for all of its work. I haven't compiled it or run any tests. `mvn -o compile` on the client module failed to resolve the `resteasy-reactive-common` 999-SNAPSHOT dependency, so I didn't confirm that `Context.executeBlocking(Callable, boolean)` exists in the Vert.x version in use. I also didn't reproduce the exception with the linked project.

My diagnosis is a guess. The old code called `vertx.getOrCreateContext()` for the `InboundBuffer` and `vertx.executeBlocking`/`vertx.runOnContext` for the reads. Those calls can end up on a different context than the one that issued the request. That could leave the response completing on an event-loop context, where a later blocking call (like a database write) throws `BlockingOperationNotAllowedException`.

The new code uses that single context for the `InboundBuffer`, `context.executeBlocking(...)` and `context.runOnContext(...)`, so the response should stay on the caller's context. I did not touch the multipart `MultiByteHttpData` path.

I didn't use the axiomengine graph. The hook said no graph was built, and I never indexed.
